label: sec:nucleon-derivation-intro
html: Because every interaction factors into elementary two-strand crossings, one begins by defining the two fundamental crossing observables on a braid word: the crossing energy E_\times and its orientation-odd component, the Coulomb charge Q. Applying linear-programming operator selection to the two-photon pair-production vertex selects the three-strand Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 \in H_3(q) as the confinement optimum. Closing the four-term photon braid with \mathcal{B}_3 yields the proton and neutron normal forms independently of the incoming photon polarization, completing the constructive chain \gamma\gamma \to q\bar{q} \to \mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n} \to \mathcal{A}(Z, N).
